candidates.source_attribution: Jubilees 33:2 (Reuben's incest (33:2)), trans. R.H. Charles, The Book of Jubilees (Oxford: Clarendon, 1902). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And Reuben saw Bilhah, Rachel's handmaid, the concubine of his father, bathing in water in a secret place, and he loved her. And he hid himself at night, and he entered the house of Bilhah at night, and he found her sleeping alone on a bed in her house. And he lay with her, and she awoke and saw, and behold Reuben was lying with her in the bed' — Jubilees preserves the Gen 35:22 incident in painful detail. The Tewahedo penitential canon's strongest category — incest, especially with a parent's spouse or partner — finds canonical anchor here. The Tewahedo's distinctive practice of detailed-confession-by-category (the Confessor walks the penitent through specific Scripture-named sins for self-examination) draws Jub 33:2 into the canonical sin-list for the spiritual-paternal-bed category.

candidates.draft_body:

'And he came to his father Jacob, and he confessed to him that he had defiled the bed of his father; and Jacob mourned exceedingly because of him, and he smote him not, because Reuben himself had confessed to him; and he had pity on him' — Jubilees uniquely preserves Reuben's voluntary confession-to-the-father and Jacob's clemency-because-of-confession. The Tewahedo confession-and-absolution pattern (näsḫa) draws on this verse for the canonical principle that voluntary disclosure to the spiritual father materially mitigates the punitive disciplinary response, even where the sin's gravity is unchanged. The 'smote him not because Reuben had confessed' clause is the Tewahedo canonical warrant for the confessor's clemency in response to genuinely-voluntary admission.

'And Reuben was not pardoned in heaven, because he was older than Joseph, and because he should not have done this thing — for he could have known that his father had her, but he loved her not as his sister' — Jubilees distinguishes terrestrial pardon (Jacob's clemency) from heavenly judicial-reckoning. Tewahedo theological precision: divine pardon and disciplinary-canonical pardon are NOT identical; the priest can absolve from canonical penalty (Heb. nash'a; Tewahedo näsḫa) without thereby exhausting the heavenly judicial dimension, which remains the Lord's. The Tewahedo's distinct doctrine on the limits of priestly absolution (against the maximalist Catholic plenary-indulgence model) draws canonical anchor here.
